subject: Discovery: Lumenix audit trail, retention & redaction requirements
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie@lumenixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — audit trail, redaction & retention (next steps)

Hi Sophie — great to meet you and the DPO team earlier. Quick recap from our side so we can align expectations and surface any gaps before the technical workshop.

Key pain you stated
- Need guaranteed deletion windows for PHI-derived tokens and model inputs/outputs (clinical notes, transcripts).
- Auditability required for every inference (who/what/when/which model version).
- Must support redaction or token-level suppression for specific PHI categories before logs are stored.

Current stack you described
- Ingest via internal API gateway -> data enters a VPC-hosted service.
- Long-term storage in a HIPAA-compliant S3 bucket with lifecycle rules.
- KMS-managed keys via AWS KMS (Customer master keys).

Your success criteria (from call)
- Retention windows configurable per environment (dev=7d, prod=90d, legal-hold exceptions).
- Immutable audit trail for every request with retention 7 years (read-only access controls, exportability).
- Ability to redact/hide PII at the earliest possible stage (either client-side redaction or server-side before logs persist).
- Evidence of SOC 2 controls and a BAA in place before pilot.

What we can provide (high-level)
- Redwood Private or Dedicated can run in your VPC/on-prem to keep inference control-plane and KV caches behind your network.
- Configurable token-level logging: you can enable prefix-only logs, full logs, or redaction filters. We support custom redaction pipelines (regex + ML labeler) and can emit sanitized vs. raw results into separate sinks.
- Audit logs include request_id, model_version, start_time, end_time, user_id, route, latency, and byte counts. Exportable to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/HTTP).
- We support CMKs and HSM-backed key management for encryption at rest.
- We have a SOC 2 summary and a standard BAA template — attaching a short SOC 2 summary and redaction-specs PDF.

Open questions for the technical workshop
1) Which fields in your request payload are considered PHI and must be redacted versus allowed in logs? (e.g., MRN, patient name, clinical observations)
2) Do you require client-side (SDK) redaction or is server-side redaction acceptable if validated by you?
3) For audit exports: is JSON Lines to S3 acceptable, or do you need streaming to an on-prem SIEM?
4) Legal-hold cases: how often do you expect to escalate and what is the process for lifting retention policies?

Proposed next steps
- Schedule 90-minute technical workshop with Lumenix infra + DPO + our infra and security leads (suggested window: Thurs 14 Jan or Mon 18 Jan).
- Pre-work: please share an anonymized sample request payload (PII can be masked) and the list of fields to preserve vs redact.
- We’ll prepare a short architecture doc showing where redaction and auditing hooks can be enforced.

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with meeting invites and a draft agenda. If any of the bullets above misstate what you covered, flag it and I’ll update.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0172

Attachments: redaction-specs.pdf (1 page summary), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (2 pages)

From: Sophie Turner <sophie@lumenixhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: DPO Team <dpo@lumenixhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — audit trail, redaction & retention (next steps)

Thanks Ben — this is a helpful summary and matches our conversation. A couple clarifications from the DPO side: 

- PHI fields we must redact from logs unless explicitly allowed: patient_name, patient_ssn, mrn, phone_number, full_address. Clinical observations can be logged if de-identified (hashing or tokenization acceptable).
- Server-side redaction is acceptable if we can review the redaction rules and run a QA pass on a sample dataset prior to enabling production logging.
- For audit exports, S3 JSON Lines is fine as long as the bucket is in our account and we can apply lifecycle + access policies.
- Legal hold: we generally trigger ~1-3 holds per year, process is manual but needs to be enforceable for records in both logs and long-term storage.

We are available Thurs 14 Jan 11:00–12:30 PT for the workshop. Please include any security engineer who will talk about KMS/HSM and the engineer who owns your redaction pipeline.

Sophie Turner
Head of Data Protection | Lumenix Health
sophie@lumenixhealth.com

See you Thursday — appreciate the quick turnaround here.
